$comment: HAND-EDITED source of the app-wide key style and shortcut layout settings (design/keyboard-style.md); gen-settings-sources.py writes the Swift descriptors and parser constants. The keys each choice adds and how a layout matches shortcuts live in schemas/keymap/key-styles.json, read by cmux-tui/crates/cmux-keymap and webviews/src/ui/keyStyle.ts. Row fields: see schemas/settings/source/updates.json.

lists.name: keyStyle
lists.note: Settings > Keyboard, first card (Leo 2026-11-16: vim or not, dvorak). Parsed by KeyboardStyleSettings.

rows.note: The keys lists answer to (sidebar, palette results, chat list, Settings lists, New Tab): Vim adds hjkl, gg, G, / and Esc, and turns on browser.vimKeys; Emacs adds Control-N, P, F, B, A and E. Text fields keep normal typing.

help.text: Vim moves through lists with j, k, gg, G and /. Emacs uses Control-N, P, F, B, A and E.

rows.note: How a shortcut finds its key: followLayout is the character the layout types (Cmd-Z is the key that types Z, today's behavior); qwertyPositions is the US key position, so Dvorak, Colemak, AZERTY and QWERTZ keep QWERTY muscle memory.

help.text: Keep QWERTY Positions puts shortcuts on the US keys, for Dvorak, Colemak, AZERTY and QWERTZ.
